system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

Drug: omega-3 fatty acids ()

Verdict: {"outcome": "failure", "outcome_basis": "readout: \"A total of 1,617 participants were diagnosed with cancer by the end of the study; 793 had been taking vitamin D and 824 had been taking the \" (announcement:vital_omega3)", "predicted_outcome": "not_computable", "consistency": "", "primary_category": "design_or_endpoint", "secondary_categories": ["population"], "calculator_category": "insufficient_data", "confidence": "high", "verification": "done", "probability_of_success": null, "weakest_link": "triglycerides change not measured"}

Hypotheses: {"hypotheses": [{"category": "design_or_endpoint", "status": "supported", "for": [{"text": "Primary endpoint is composite MACE (heart attack, stroke, etc.). Readout states 'omega-3 fish oil reduced heart attack rates but did not affect risk of stroke' (f_29ceec807e9773). Heart attack events: 145 vs 200 (HR ~0.725, f_ebecb5ff5c1a38, f_4f58107821651d). Total MACE events: 386 vs 419 (HR ~0.92, f_0c375ad1e96692, f_a69c1125c7928c). The neutral stroke component dilutes the composite, pushing HR from ~0.72 to ~0.92, above the trial's MDE HR of 0.821 at 80% power (calculator).", "refs": ["f_29ceec807e9773", "f_ebecb5ff5c1a38", "f_4f58107821651d", "f_0c375ad1e96692", "f_a69c1125c7928c", "calculator"]}], "against": [{"text": "Composite endpoints are standard in CVOTs; the trial was designed to detect a broad cardiovascular benefit.", "refs": ["f_73c247f2636a41", "f_953274be216910"]}], "would_settle": "Component-specific HRs and CIs for MI, stroke, and CV death from the primary publication."}, {"category": "population", "status": "supported", "for": [{"text": "Primary prevention population (age ≥50, generally healthy, f_eff2147f4c4bca). Low event rate (805 MACE in 25,871 over 5.3 years, f_e86c988bd18828, f_4654581125e7cc). Omega-3's putative mechanisms (anti-arrhythmic, plaque stabilization, triglyceride lowering) may preferentially reduce sudden death/MI but not stroke or other MACE components in this lower-risk group. In secondary prevention trials (e.g., GISSI-P, JELIS), omega-3 showed larger composite benefits.", "refs": ["f_eff2147f4c4bca", "f_e86c988bd18828", "f_4654581125e7cc", "f_29ceec807e9773"]}], "against": [{"text": "Primary prevention is the intended use case for a supplement; the trial population matches the target population.", "refs": ["f_73c247f2636a41"]}], "would_settle": "Meta-analysis of omega-3 trials stratified by primary vs secondary prevention and by endpoint components."}, {"category": "biomarker_not_causal", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "Intended biomarker is triglycerides. Reference table lists triglycerides causal=uncertain (but triglycerides via apoB causal=yes). Omega-3 lowers triglycerides but may not lower apoB proportionally. No on-treatment triglyceride change measured in VITAL (calculator weakest_link).", "refs": ["calculator", "f_fdcf156c06d8c9"]}], "against": [{"text": "Omega-3 has multiple mechanisms beyond triglycerides (anti-inflammatory, membrane stabilization, anti-arrhythmic). The heart attack reduction suggests some causal pathway is engaged. Triglyceride causality is uncertain, not definitively non-causal.", "refs": ["f_29ceec807e9773"]}], "would_settle": "On-treatment triglyceride and apoB changes in VITAL or a similar primary prevention population."}, {"category": "effect_too_small", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "For the composite MACE endpoint, observed HR ~0.92 exceeds the MDE HR of 0.821 (calculator), so the effect on the chosen endpoint was too small to detect with 805 events.", "refs": ["calculator", "f_0c375ad1e96692", "f_a69c1125c7928c"]}], "against": [{"text": "The biological effect on heart attacks (HR ~0.72) is large and clinically meaningful. The 'effect too small' applies to the diluted composite endpoint, not the underlying mechanism.", "refs": ["f_29ceec807e9773", "f_ebecb5ff5c1a38", "f_4f58107821651d"]}], "would_settle": "Larger trial or meta-analysis focused on MI as primary endpoint."}, {"category": "target_not_causal", "status": "undetermined", "for": [{"text": "Omega-3 fatty acids act through multiple pathways; no single molecular target. Genetics evidence for coronary artery disorder is absent (target_genetics: uncertain).", "refs": ["calculator"]}], "against": [{"text": "Lack of a single target does not imply non-causality; the observed MI reduction suggests biological activity.", "refs": ["f_29ceec807e9773"]}], "would_settle": "Mendelian randomization studies of lifelong omega-3 exposure or triglyceride-lowering variants on MI vs stroke."}, {"category": "off_target_harm", "status": "weakened", "for": [], "against": [{"text": "No serious side effects reported: 'No serious side effects, such as bleeding, high blood calcium levels, or gastrointestinal symptoms were found with either supplement' (f_f748786928e43a).", "refs": ["f_f748786928e43a"]}], "would_settle": "Detailed safety data from primary publication."}, {"category": "execution_or_nonscientific", "status": "weakened", "for": [], "against": [{"text": "Large, well-conducted trial: 25,871 randomized, 5.3-year median follow-up, low dropout implied by event counts. No adherence or recruitment issues reported.", "refs": ["f_4654581125e7cc", "f_1bc90d2278fe91", "f_a01a7f3db2f2b4"]}], "would_settle": "Adherence data from primary publication."}, {"category": "insufficient_data", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "Calculator could not compute expected HR because no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change from VITAL was available (calculator weakest_link: 'triglycerides change not measured').", "refs": ["calculator"]}], "against": [{"text": "Verified facts provide clear outcome data (component-specific event counts, readout statement) enabling a mechanistic diagnosis (endpoint dilution) without biomarker change data.", "refs": ["f_29ceec807e9773", "f_ebecb5ff5c1a38", "f_4f58107821651d", "f_0c375ad1e96692", "f_a69c1125c7928c"]}], "would_settle": "Publication of on-treatment lipid biomarkers from VITAL."}], "primary_category": "design_or_endpoint", "secondary_categories": ["population"], "confidence": "high", "departure_from_calculator": "Calculator returned 'insufficient_data' due to missing on-treatment triglyceride change. However, verified facts reveal a clear pattern: significant reduction in heart attacks (HR ~0.72) but no effect on stroke, causing the composite MACE endpoint (HR ~0.92) to miss significance. This endpoint dilution is a design_or_endpoint issue, not insufficient data. The trial's MDE HR at 80% power was 0.821 (calculator); the observed composite HR ~0.92 exceeds this because the benefit was confined to one component."}

response:
{
  "headline": "VITAL's omega-3 arm failed its primary composite MACE endpoint (HR ~0.92) despite reducing heart attacks (HR ~0.72), because the neutral stroke component diluted the composite above the trial's minimum detectable effect.",
  "summary": "VITAL randomized 25,871 participants aged 50 and older and followed them for a median of 5.3 years, accruing 805 major adverse cardiovascular events. The primary composite of heart attack or stroke was neutral: 386 events on omega-3 versus 419 on control (HR ~0.92). However, heart attacks were reduced (145 versus 200; HR ~0.72) while stroke was unaffected, so the composite endpoint diluted the benefit and stayed above the trial's MDE HR of 0.821 at 80% power. Confidence is high: the trial was large, well conducted, and reported no serious side effects.",
  "key_evidence": [
    "25,871 participants randomized; median follow-up 5.3 years — VITAL Study Reveals How Vitamin D and Fish Oil Supplements Affect Risk of Heart Attack, Stroke and Cancer; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01169259 VITAL",
    "805 total major adverse cardiovascular events — VITAL Study Reveals How Vitamin D and Fish Oil Supplements Affect Risk of Heart Attack, Stroke and Cancer",
    "Primary composite MACE: 386 treatment vs 419 control events (HR ~0.92) — VITAL Study Reveals How Vitamin D and Fish Oil Supplements Affect Risk of Heart Attack, Stroke and Cancer",
    "Heart attacks: 145 treatment vs 200 control (HR ~0.72) — VITAL Study Reveals How Vitamin D and Fish Oil Supplements Affect Risk of Heart Attack, Stroke and Cancer",
    "Readout: omega-3 fish oil reduced heart attack rates but did not affect risk of stroke or cancer — VITAL Study Reveals How Vitamin D and Fish Oil Supplements Affect Risk of Heart Attack, Stroke and Cancer",
    "Minimum detectable effect HR 0.821 at 80% power; composite HR ~0.92 exceeds this — calculator"
  ],
  "what_would_change_this": "Component-specific HRs and confidence intervals for myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death from the primary publication would confirm whether the heart-attack benefit is real and whether the composite null was purely endpoint dilution. On-treatment triglyceride and apoB changes would clarify the biomarker pathway.",
  "readthrough_note": "Secondary-prevention omega-3 programmes such as GISSI-P and JELIS showed larger composite benefits, suggesting VITAL's null composite may reflect its lower-risk primary-prevention population rather than absence of biological activity."
}
